comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: Contract tests cover both modes. Deployed; changelog notes the default atomic behavior.

content.text: Contract tests cover both modes. Deployed; changelog notes the default atomic behavior.

POST /v2/issues/bulk-update accepts a batch whose issue keys span multiple projects and applies updates to the subset the caller can write, committing partial success without an error envelope. Callers believe the whole batch applied.

Expected: either reject the batch with 400 when project keys mix under a single-project token, or return a per-item result set with committed/failed flags. Actual: the handler filters unauthorized or cross-project items silently and returns 200 with only the committed ids in the response body, omitting failures.
Hypothesis: authorization is applied per item after the transaction starts, and failed items are skipped without accumulating a failure list. The outer transaction still commits successful rows.
Automation scripts that move status across a program of projects end up with half-applied migrations and no signal to retry the rest.
